$comment: scripts/check-neutral-names.mjs reads this. The base product's old role word has no section here: it is allowed nowhere (scripts/lib/neutral-names.mjs). record_words is the ratchet for the record words written as prose (scripts/lib/record-words.mjs): which files are read, the names that are not prose, and a per-file ceiling for what remains.

record_words.$comment: The record words (customer, deployment, implementation, rollout; any case, singular or plural) written as PROSE in text base code hands to a reader: string literals, template text and JSX text of source files, Markdown, the string values of JSON. Base text writes a placeholder the profile fills instead ({account}, {deployment}, {implementation}, {rollout}; agent/lib/agent-vocabulary.ts) or takes the word from lib/ui-words.ts. Identifiers, paths, code spans, quoted values and one-token strings are never counted. `node scripts/check-neutral-names.mjs --records --lines` lists what is left.

scan.$comment: Globs of the files read. Everything a model or a person is handed by base code; not docs, tests, comments or migrations.
scan.agent/**: the agent: prompts, tool and parameter descriptions, messages, skills and sandbox files
scan.app/**: the web app and its API messages
scan.lib/**: server and client libraries whose strings reach a page, an API answer or a seeded file
scan.skills/**: the base skill a coding assistant installs
scan.setup/skills/**: the base skill as the generic package ships it (filled from the default profile)
scan.scripts/seed*: the seeders: what a new data room and a demo database are filled with
scan.profiles/00-default.json: the default profile: the words every placeholder is filled with
scan.dm.md: the data-room description served to coding assistants
scan.library/**/workflows/**: the library workflows: their prompts write the placeholders the profile fills

skip.$comment: Globs left out of the scan, each for a reason.
skip.**/*.generated.*: derived from a scanned source (prompts, the profile, the workflow library, the subagent registry)
skip.agent/lib/agent-vocabulary.ts: the vocabulary machinery: it names the legacy words to translate them (LEGACY_RECORDS) and its comments' examples are not text anyone is handed
skip.**/__fixtures__/**: fixture records: stored data, not base text

names.$comment: Whole names that are not prose where they stand: a specialist's directory name (hyphenated anywhere; a single word only when written **bold** or as code), and stored enum values and sheet names of more than one word. Each is a contract.
names.customer-context: specialist directory name: the model delegates to it by this name
names.deployment: specialist directory name (allowed as **deployment** in a roster line)
names.customer-vpc: stored enum value (deployment region / hosting model)
names.Customer Stakeholders: workbook sheet name (People/Master.xlsx), a contract of the data model
names.new-customer: npm script and operator tool name (operator:new-customer), a contract (scripts/test-operator-tooling.mjs)

ceilings.$comment: Per file, the exact count of record words written as prose today, grouped by why they remain. More fails; fewer fails with the number to lower it to; a ceiling on a file that carries none fails. The agent side (prompts, tool and parameter descriptions, messages, the library workflows, the base skill, the default profile, the operator tooling) carries none: PR 7a. A data-room domain's name is no exception any more (mold_v1-148): its folder is the deployment profile's, base text writes it as a placeholder ({domain:accounts}), and a capitalised record word in a sentence is counted like any other.

stored.why: A stored enum value that is the record word itself (`blockerOwner: "Customer"`, a ticket's waiting party). Rows are never rewritten here: changing a stored value is a data migration. A relabelling profile's reader gets the profile's label for it (domains.<area>.fields.<key>.options).

ui.why: The web app, its API messages and the libraries behind them (app/, components/, lib/): PR 7b of mold_v1-103 owns these and lowers each ceiling as it takes the word from lib/ui-words.ts (W.account, W.deployments, …) or fills a placeholder. Counted at the commit PR 7a branched from.

seeders.why: The seeders (scripts/seed*): the sample data room and demo database they write. PR 7b of mold_v1-103 owns these; sample CONTENT (a fictional account's notes) is data and may stay under its ceiling, the seeders' own labels and messages move to the profile's words.

third_party.why: Another product's own word for what it syncs, on that product's connector card: the Vercel card lists Vercel's "Deployments" beside its build logs and regions. It names the third party's builds, not this product's record area, and is the same under every profile. Counted since a data-room domain's former folder name stopped being an exception (mold_v1-148): before that the word was passed over as "a stored folder name".

stored_folders.$comment: The data-room folder names (the names the folders had while they were written into the code, scripts/lib/legacy-dataroom-folders.json, and the default profile's) spelled in base code: as the head of a path anywhere in a file, comments included, or as a string that is exactly a name. Base code builds a path from FOLDER.<id> (agent/lib/dataroom-folders.ts) and base text writes {folder:<id>} or {domain:<id>}, so the names are the deployment profile's and a deployment that already holds files keeps them by pinning. `node scripts/check-neutral-names.mjs --folders --lines` lists what is left.

scan.$comment: Globs of the files read: everything that runs, ships or is handed to a reader, and the tests and checks that exercise it.
scan.agent/**: the agent: tools, stores, prompts, skills and sandbox files
scan.app/**: the web app and its API routes
scan.skills/**: the base skill a coding assistant installs
scan.setup/**: the package a coding agent installs: its tools and hosts
scan.scripts/**: the seeders, the operator tooling, the library workflows, the generators, the checks and the tests
scan.dm.md: the data-room description served to coding assistants
scan..claude/**: the skills, agents and scripts a coding agent follows in this repository (the eve-* subagent skills a pack author copies paths from included): a path written there is copied into a pack's subagent.json or an operator run, so it is written {folder:<id>}
scan.*.md: the root instructions a coding agent reads first (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md)

values_in.$comment: Globs, within the scan, of the files whose string literals are also read for a value that is exactly a folder name: the code that runs or ships. A test's or a check's strings are read for path heads only (a string that is exactly one of these words there is the word: a record area's label, a heading).
values_in.app/**: the web app and its API routes
values_in.setup/**: the package a coding agent installs

skip.$comment: Globs left out of the scan, each for a reason.
skip.**/*.generated.*: derived from a scanned source and the profile (the profile itself, the prompts, the registry, the workflow library, the package's deployment module)
skip.scripts/lib/legacy-dataroom-folders.json: THE ONE LEGACY DEFINITION: the names the folders had while they were written into the code
skip.setup/dm.md: the generic package's dm.md: generated from dm.md and the default profile (npm run build:agent-cli -- --write-default)
skip.setup/skills/**: the base skill as the generic package ships it: generated from skills/ and the default profile
skip.scripts/fixtures/**: pinned before-images and profile fixtures: what a deployment read and stored before folder names were a profile setting, kept verbatim so the tests can prove a pinned profile against it

ceilings.$comment: Per file, the exact count of folder names spelled today, grouped by why they remain. More fails; fewer fails with the number to lower it to; a ceiling on a file that spells none fails.

placeholder_keys.why: The record placeholders' own keys ({Accounts}, {Deployments}, {Implementation}; RECORD_KEYS): the capitalised plural of a record WORD, which is what base text writes to have the profile's word filled in. Words of the placeholder grammar, never a folder: a path is built from FOLDER.<id> and a folder is written {folder:<id>}.

third_party.why: Another product's own word for what it syncs, on that product's connector card (Salesforce's "Accounts", Vercel's "Deployments"): the third party's objects, the same under every profile, never a data-room folder.

roster.why: The workspace's own People tab and the roster workbook's sheet (Workspace > People > Import roster): the members of the workspace. Not the data room's people domain, whose folder and label come from the profile.

builtin_library.$comment: Base code ships no workflow, no recipe and no starter app of its own: what a workspace is provisioned with is the deployment profile's (library.sources; scripts/lib/builtin-library.mjs says what is checked). libraries: where a library's content may live. skip: tests and pinned fixtures, which never run in a deployment. writers: every source file that inserts into the workflows, recipes or apps table, each with what decides its rows; a new one fails until it is listed here with its reason, and one that stops inserting fails until it is removed.

libraries.library/**: the library directories a deployment profile names under library.sources (workflows/*.workflow.js, recipes.json, apps.json, history.json)

skip.scripts/fixtures/**: pinned before-images, among them the built-ins base code carried before the library became the profile's
skip.scripts/test-*.mjs: tests insert the rows they then assert on, in throwaway workspaces
skip.scripts/lib/builtin-library.mjs: this check, which has to describe what it matches
skip.services/**: the task-workflow service: its own tables and tests, no workspace library

writers.agent/lib/app-tools.ts: create_app: one app a person asked the agent for, approved by them
writers.agent/lib/provision-workspace.ts: a new workspace: the deployment profile's library (recipes, workflows and starter apps, none by default) and one row per specialist of the generated registry, minus the ones the profile excludes
writers.app/api/ops/apps/route.ts: POST /api/ops/apps: one app a signed-in person asked for
writers.app/api/ops/workflows/route.ts: POST /api/ops/workflows: one row a signed-in person asked for
writers.scripts/operator/seed-workflows.mjs: operator:seed-workflows: the deployment profile's library into a workspace an operator names; nothing when the profile names none
writers.scripts/seed-ops.mjs: a legacy local demo seeder in no npm script, kept for its --print test: its rows carry no org_id, which the NOT NULL column refuses, so it cannot write to a current database

period_words.$comment: What a work period is called is the deployment profile's (work_periods.label; agent/lib/work-periods.ts). The default profile's word for it (read from profiles/00-default.json by scripts/lib/period-words.mjs, never spelled there) may appear only: in the default profile and the modules generated from it (default_profile); in ONE legacy definition, with an exact count (legacy_definition); inside a listed contract, a pattern for an exact name something outside this repository already holds, optionally limited to the files it may appear in (contracts); or under an exempt path (exempt_paths). Anything else fails check:neutral-names.

default_profile.profiles/00-default.json: The default profile: work_periods.label is where the word lives.
default_profile.lib/deployment-profile.generated.ts: Generated from profiles/*.json (the web app's copy of the merged profile).
default_profile.agent/lib/deployment-profile.generated.t: Generated from profiles/*.json (the agent's copy of the merged profile).
default_profile.setup/deployment.generated.mjs: Generated from the default profile: the generic coding-agent package's settings (workPeriods.label).

legacy_definition.why: The `cycles` table's own comment says what a cycle was in the base product's words. One sentence, kept so the stored name can be understood; it also says that nothing else spells the word.

contracts.why: The coding agent's two period tools, by their wire names: a saved MCP configuration and a published package call them. Their descriptions take the profile's word; a rename would be an additive alias (setup/workspace-tools.mjs `aliases`), never a replacement.
The period view's key in a Todos deep link (/?ops=todos&view=…): links people already shared carry it. It is a key, defined once (PERIOD_VIEW in lib/work-periods-ui.ts), never a label.

A workflow of the account-delivery library, by its stored name (workflows.name in every workspace provisioned with that library). It names a readiness push, not a work period; the library itself is exempt below.

exempt_paths.drizzle/: Migration history and its snapshots: never rewritten.
exempt_paths.library/: A library a deployment profile opts into (library.sources) is that library's own content, in its own line of work's words: not base text.
exempt_paths.scripts/fixtures/: Recorded before-images of what a default deployment's model and pages read, and test fixtures: they hold the default profile's word because the default deployment reads it.
exempt_paths..migrate-cycles.mjs: A one-off migration script that already ran: history.
exempt_paths..migrate-cycles-lead.mjs: A one-off migration script that already ran: history.
exempt_paths..migrate-workspace-v2.mjs: A one-off migration script that already ran: history.
exempt_paths.data/sample/: The local demo's sample records: data, never shipped as product text (scripts/test-sample-data.mjs holds that).
